strings.d1.s0.name: Taipei 101 Observatory
strings.d1.s0.tips: 89th floor; the first slot in the morning is uncrowded. See the wind damper ball.
strings.d1.s1.name: Xinyi District
strings.d1.s1.tips: Shopping malls and the Eslite bookshop; air-conditioned.
strings.d1.s2.name: Din Tai Fung Xinyi
strings.d1.s2.tips: The brand where xiaolongbao (soup dumplings) was born; take a queue number at 11:45.
strings.d1.s3.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
strings.d1.s3.tips: Changing of the guard every hour; park with a view of Taipei 101.
strings.d1.s4.name: Elephant Mountain
strings.d1.s4.tips: 20 minutes of steep steps; the sunset photo of Taipei 101, crowded but worth it.
strings.d1.b0.name: Kao Chi Yongkang
strings.d1.b0.tips: A cheaper rival to Din Tai Fung; xiaolongbao.
strings.d1.b1.name: Songshan Cultural Park
strings.d1.b1.tips: Design exhibitions in an old tobacco factory.
strings.d2.s0.name: National Palace Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: Imperial Chinese treasures, including the jadeite cabbage and the meat-shaped stone. Go Tuesday to Saturday and get in before the morning tour buses arrive.
strings.d2.s1.name: Shilin Official Residence
strings.d2.s1.tips: Gardens of Chiang Kai-shek's residence; rose garden.
strings.d2.s2.name: Lin Dong Fang Beef Noodle
strings.d2.s2.tips: Taipei's best beef noodle soup (Bib Gourmand); clear broth.
strings.d2.s3.name: Beitou Thermal Valley
strings.d2.s3.tips: Steaming green thermal lake; smell of sulphur, MRT Xinbeitou.
strings.d2.s4.name: Beitou Public Hot Spring
strings.d2.s4.tips: Public hot spring (60 TWD, swimsuit required); you'll be among locals.
strings.d2.b0.name: Shilin Night Market
strings.d2.b0.tips: Taipei's biggest night market; giant fried chicken cutlet and stinky tofu.
strings.d2.b1.name: Beitou Hot Spring Museum
strings.d2.b1.tips: Japanese-era bathhouse building; go on a rainy day.
strings.d3.s0.name: Yehliu Geopark
strings.d3.s0.tips: Queen's Head rock and mushroom rocks; arrive before the morning tour buses.
strings.d3.s1.name: Shifen Waterfall
strings.d3.s2.name: Shifen Old Street
strings.d3.s2.tips: Release a wish lantern over the railway (150 TWD); watch the train pass.
strings.d3.s3.name: Jiufen Old Street
strings.d3.s3.tips: Terraced mountain town; taro balls and tea houses, with a Spirited Away feel.
strings.d3.s4.name: A-Mei Tea House Jiufen
strings.d3.s4.tips: Tea house with red lanterns; oolong and views, and the lanterns light up at sunset.
strings.d3.b0.name: Jiufen Grandma Lai Taro Ball
strings.d3.b1.name: Houtong Cat Village
strings.d3.b1.tips: Cat village; an alternative to Shifen.
strings.d4.s0.name: Longshan Temple
strings.d4.s0.tips: Taipei's oldest temple; morning prayers, incense and divination blocks.
strings.d4.s1.name: Bopiliao Historic Block
strings.d4.s2.name: Dihua Street
strings.d4.s2.tips: Dadaocheng's street of dried goods and tea; Baroque facades, Chinese New Year market.
strings.d4.s3.name: Yongle Market Food Court
strings.d4.s3.tips: Local food in the Dadaocheng market; oyster omelette.
strings.d4.s4.name: Dadaocheng Wharf
strings.d4.s4.tips: Riverside container bars; sunset and cycling.
strings.d4.b0.name: Du Hsiao Yueh Taipei
strings.d4.b1.name: Ximending
strings.d4.b1.tips: Taipei's Shibuya; youth culture and street art, an alternative to the wharf.
strings.d5.s0.name: Maokong Gondola
strings.d5.s0.tips: Glass-bottom gondola from Zoo station; tea gardens at the top.
strings.d5.s1.name: Maokong Çay Evi
strings.d5.s1.tips: Oolong tea and tea-based dishes at the top; views of Taipei.
strings.d5.s2.name: Taipei Zoo
strings.d5.s3.name: Zhinan Temple
strings.d5.s3.tips: Taoist temple on the mountain; gondola middle station.
strings.d5.s4.name: Raohe Night Market
strings.d5.s4.tips: Single-street night market; at the entrance, charcoal-baked pepper buns (Fuzhou pepper bun).
strings.d5.b0.name: Ningxia Night Market
strings.d5.b1.name: Bitan Scenic Area
strings.d5.b1.tips: Lake and suspension bridge in Xindian; boats.
strings.d6.s0.name: Tamsui Old Street
strings.d6.s0.tips: End of the MRT line; estuary town, a-gei (stuffed tofu) and fish balls.
strings.d6.s1.name: Fort San Domingo
strings.d6.s1.tips: Dutch-Spanish fort and British consulate; red building.
strings.d6.s2.name: Tamsui A-Gei Lokantası
strings.d6.s2.tips: Glass noodles inside tofu; Tamsui's signature dish.
strings.d6.s3.name: Fisherman's Wharf Tamsui
strings.d6.s3.tips: Lovers' Bridge; reached by ferry, pier cafés.
strings.d6.s4.name: Tamsui Gün Batımı Sahili
strings.d6.s4.tips: One of Taiwan's most famous sunsets; river mouth.
strings.d6.b0.name: Tamsui Zhengzhong Fish Ball
strings.d6.b1.name: Bali Left Bank
strings.d6.b1.tips: Ferry to the opposite bank; cycle path.
strings.d7.s0.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
strings.d7.s0.tips: Giant white monument and changing of the guard (every hour); Liberty Square.
strings.d7.s1.name: Yongkang Street
strings.d7.s1.tips: Cafés and mango shaved ice; Smoothie House.
strings.d7.s2.name: Yongkang Beef Noodle
strings.d7.s2.tips: Beef noodles with seared beef since 1963; farewell lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: Da'an Forest Park
strings.d7.s3.tips: City forest; last walk. 40 minutes by MRT to Taoyuan Airport.
strings.d7.b0.name: Smoothie House Yongkang
strings.d7.b0.tips: Mango snow ice; a dessert instead of noodles.
strings.d7.b1.name: Taipei Botanical Garden
strings.d7.b1.tips: Lotus ponds; an alternative to the park.
strings.note0: The EasyCard works on the MRT, buses and YouBike; eating and drinking are banned on the MRT (fines apply). It takes 40 minutes by MRT to Taoyuan Airport.
strings.note1: October to December is the best season (22-26°C). January and February are 12-15°C and rainy, but it is hot spring season. Shops are closed over Chinese New Year.
strings.note2: Night markets are open 18:00-24:00; 300 TWD is enough to eat your fill. No tipping, and cash is still common.
strings.note3: For Jiufen, Shifen and Yehliu take a tour (~1,500 TWD) or the 1062 bus; go to Jiufen in the afternoon, as the lanterns light up after 17:00.
strings.note4: Take a queue number at Din Tai Fung; in Yongkang, Lin Dong Fang noodles cost 250 TWD.
strings.note5: Shoes are not taken off in temples; divination blocks and incense are allowed.
strings.transit.name: EasyCard
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on the MRT, buses, YouBike and in shops, including the Jiufen bus.
